summary: Built GO-LIVE step 3: a real SMTP sender that cannot send by default. All three gates (--live, complete env config, explicit --cap N) route through one chokepoint, send.live_blockers(); any failure names the gate, shows the send-free preview, exits 2. Added the `sends` ledger to db.py (claim_send/mark_send/sent_today_count/send_state) enabling record-before-send idempotency and a cap counted from what actually went out today. Full checklist implemented: send-time DNC re-check per lead, forward-only status advance, asserted CAN-SPAM footer, and a `stop` kill switch re-read before every message. The SMTP transport is constructed only inside the all-gates-passed branch, and tests/conftest.py poisons smtplib.SMTP/SMTP_SSL suite-wide so any accidental real connection is a hard test failure rather than an email. FOUND AND FIXED A REAL BUG that all tests missed: the cap is computed on every run, so on the operator's real pre-ledger DB even a plain dry-run crashed with 'no such table: sends' — fixtures calling init_db hid it. Wrote the regression test first (confirmed failing), then made sent_today_count return 0 when the ledger is absent, keeping dry-run strictly read-only rather than migrating the operator's DB to preview (verified: real DB still has no sends table after two dry-runs). ESCALATION: the sends table is a DB schema change (AGENTS.md escalation), authorized by Kerry's Q3 answer since idempotency requires persistence; additive only, flagged in GO-LIVE.md as still owing an independent review. AGENTS.md is the one file outside the approved plan's seven — appended the two mistakes I made to its 'Known Agent Mistakes' section, which explicitly invites that. Nothing was sent; no commits; kill switch left released.

Addressed all four MUST-FIX review findings, each with a regression test written first and observed failing before the fix (17 initially failing, all now passing).

Finding 1 (db.py sent_today_count): now counts EVERY claim made today regardless of state, not just claimed/sent. The sender treats a transport exception as possibly-delivered (hence keeping the claim and never retrying), so an ambiguous 'failed' row must consume the cap too — otherwise a post-delivery exception frees a slot and the daily cap can be exceeded. Test: test_failed_send_consumes_a_daily_slot.

Finding 2 (send.py _effective_cap): changed min(--cap, daily) - sent_today to min(--cap, daily_remaining). The daily allowance is spent down by earlier runs; --cap bounds only this run. daily=20, --cap=5, 1 prior send now permits 5 (was 4). Tests: test_run_cap_is_not_reduced_by_earlier_sends, test_daily_allowance_still_bounds_the_run_cap.

Finding 3 (config.py): smtp_port changed from `int = 587` to `int | None = None` — the 587 default meant the live gate could never report SMTP_PORT unset, silently passing on a value the operator never chose. Added _parse_port(), which never raises: unset/malformed/out-of-range reads as None, so a typo produces the required refusal + preview + exit 2 instead of a ValueError before live_blockers() could run. Verified on the real CLI both ways. Tests: test_smtp_port_is_none_when_unset, test_malformed_smtp_port_becomes_none_instead_of_raising (7 cases), test_smtp_port_parses_a_valid_value. NOTE: this is a deliberate public-API default removal on SendConfig, flagged for review; .env.example already documents SMTP_PORT=587.

Finding 4 (send.py missing_for_live): replaced raw truthiness with _present(), which strips before validating, so whitespace-only values no longer satisfy the gate — notably SENDER_ADDRESS="   " can no longer authorize a live send with no meaningful CAN-SPAM address. Also excluded bool from the port check (bool subclasses int, so True would read as port 1). Tests: test_whitespace_only_env_values_do_not_satisfy_the_gate (6 cases), test_whitespace_sender_address_cannot_authorize_a_live_send.

Also updated docs/GO-LIVE.md: three claims in it were made false by these fixes (it stated the 587 default as fact and documented the old cap formula). No other changes. Nothing was sent; no commits; kill switch released; the operator's real DB confirmed still unmigrated by dry-run.
